A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Obj-Disco research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, component ablations, a misalignment case study, and human evaluations in Sections 5 and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an expanded misalignment evaluation and original patching, SFT, dataset-selection, and reward-model comparison studies.

M1.justification: The core discovery, verification, and exemplar-selection algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix A.5.6 adds an adaptation using negative SFT loss as the reward signal, while A.5.5 introduces a workflow that edits discovered objectives, realigns with GRPO, and repeats discovery.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5.7 adds Stanford Human Preferences data, illustrated through food recommendations and legal/ethical reasoning. The original TL;DR, HH-RLHF, Alpaca, and Skywork coverage remains; the new SFT and patching studies reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: The discovery-method comparators remain Iter-Filter, Zero-Shot, Fixed-3, Fixed-15, Limited-Zero-Shot, and the existing component ablations. Fixed-15 already appeared in v1. The added reward-model comparisons vary alignment configurations rather than introduce competing discovery methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds a trial-level misalignment evaluation using gpt-4.1-mini classification. Appendices A.5.5–A.5.8 introduce corrective GRPO realignment, SFT-loss-based discovery, dataset comparisons holding the reward model fixed, and reward-model comparisons holding the dataset and policy family fixed. Existing Model-Fit and human-study protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Four new case studies examine whether discovered objectives support corrective intervention, transfer to SFT, distinguish dataset effects, and distinguish reward-model effects. The informative-sampling and fixed-objective ablations receive expanded quantitative evaluation. The original static-checkpoint comparison is retained and relocated.

E5.justification: The misalignment comparison expands from four to 34 independent trials and adds a 95% confidence interval and pairwise p-values. The patching study reports ten audit trials, and the reward-model study reports three trials per model. Existing Model-Fit uncertainty reporting and human-study statistics remain.

E6.justification: v1's four-trial summary reports detection in 3/4 Obj-Disco trials and at most 1/4 baseline trials. The expanded LLM-judged evaluation reports 58.8% for Obj-Disco, versus 20.6% Iter-Filter, 0% Zero-Shot, 23.5% Fixed-3, 44.1% Fixed-15, and 5.9% Limited-Zero-Shot. New findings include no misaligned objectives rediscovered in ten patch audits and qualitative SFT, dataset, and reward-model profiles. Existing benchmark plots and human-study results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal objective definitions, Obj-Error and Model-Fit equations, trend functions, and submodular selection guarantee remain unchanged. The SFT discussion invokes an existing supervised-learning/reinforcement-learning connection without adding a proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of interpretable reward decomposition, over 90% reward-behavior recovery, human validation, and latent-misalignment detection. The added applications appear as supplementary case studies without redefining those headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of objective patching as actionable intervention, SFT coefficient magnitudes, dataset-specific behavioral profiles, and reward-model-dependent hedging versus refusal. Appendix A.7 newly discusses checkpoint-access and storage barriers and noisy trajectories from weak instruction-following models. A.5.1 also acknowledges Fixed-15 as a more competitive comparator.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the misalignment judge and supplies its full classification prompt in Figure 10. It also documents the corrective objective, realignment workflow, and negative-SFT-loss signal. Existing discovery hyperparameters, PPO/GRPO settings, and human-study instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dineen et al.'s QA-LIGN citation and Barto and Dietterich's supervised-learning/reinforcement-learning connection. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works; the main positioning against prior discovery and interpretability approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the safety results and ablation discussion, adds four appendix subsections, and expands limitations. It also adds acknowledgements and a conflict-of-interest disclosure. The main exposition and overall section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the misalignment-judging prompt display and before/after patching display, expands Figure 3's caption, and relocates existing figures. v1 Figure 6 becomes appendix Figure 25. Existing numerical plots and hyperparameter tables are preserved without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The 34-trial safety evaluation, uncertainty reporting, explicit judging prompt, and expanded limitations improve the assessability of v1's four-trial case study. The new applications add useful exploratory evidence. Gains remain bounded: the Fixed-15 comparison is not statistically significant (p = 0.33), and the patching study establishes no rediscovered misaligned objectives rather than independently verified removal of harmful behavior.
